newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta share index down sharply.
newsitem.headline: Malta share index down sharply.

text.p: The Malta share index dropped by 11.44 points to 974.18 in the once-weekly session of the Malta Stock Exchange on Wednesday.

Stockbrokers reported relatively heavy selling of equities, possibly in anticipation of stock issues by the government. It was the first session of the exchange since the government presented its budget on Monday night.
Turnover reached just under 317,100 Maltese pounds ($856,170) from the previous week's 458,000 pounds. Trading was spread in 136 deals, of which 69 were in equities and 67 in fixed income securities.
Equities trading amounted to 170,000 pounds, with 133,323 shares changing hands.

Of these, 84,150 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 44 deals at an average price of 122 cents, down one cent. There were 17 deals in Mid-Med Bank with 36,187 shares selling for an average 147.3 cents, down from 148.7 last week.

Two deals were struck in Middle Sea Insurance with 750 shares being sold for an average 121 cents each, down four mils. Lombard Bank Malta also traded, with 8,000 shares selling for an average 140 cents per share, down four cents.

A total of 3,000 Farsons ordinary shares were sold for an average 50 cents per share, unchanged. In the 8.8 percent Farsons preference shares 1996/99, 1,236 shares were sold for 101 cents each, up three mils.
In government bonds, 19 issues were dealt in, with turnover reaching 136,500 pounds. Business was mainly in the longer term bonds, particularly the 7.5 percent MGS 2011 and the 7.25 percent MGS 2006.
In corporate bonds, three deals in the 6.5 percent Gasan Bonds reached 3,350 pounds. There were eight deals in Mid-Med Bank unsecured loan stock 2005 amounting 6,841 pounds.
